title: Antonyms
lines: Antonym questions in USAT give a word in capitals and ask for the option most opposite in meaning. They sit with synonyms in the Verbal Reasoning section. The skill is the same as for synonyms, with one extra step: after you know the meaning, you must turn it round.
- Define the stem word simply: OPTIMISTIC = expecting good things.
- Make the opposite in your own words: expecting bad things.
- Find the option that matches: pessimistic.
- Check that the other options are either unrelated or only partly opposite.
! Many wrong options are synonyms of the stem. Examiners put them in because a hurried candidate sees a familiar meaning and clicks it. Read the instruction: most opposite.
| Negative prefix un-, in-, im-, il-, ir-, dis- | able / unable, legal / illegal, regular / irregular, honest / dishonest
| Prefix pairs | include / exclude, increase / decrease, import / export, ascend / descend
| Suffix pairs | careful / careless, hopeful / hopeless
| Root pairs | benevolent / malevolent, maximum / minimum, synonym / antonym
| Separate words | ancient / modern, scarce / abundant, humble / arrogant
! Not every in- word is negative. Inflammable means easily set on fire, the same as flammable. Its opposite is non-flammable. Invaluable means extremely valuable, not worthless.
> Lethargic means sluggish and without energy, so the opposite is energetic: B. Sleepy is close to a synonym, which is the trap.
> To conceal is to hide; the opposite is to reveal, C. Hide is the synonym trap; destroy and protect are unrelated.
> An amateur does something without being paid or fully trained. The opposite is a professional, B. Beginner is close in meaning, not opposite.

When you learn a new word, learn its opposite at the same time. Write the pair side by side: generous / stingy, praise / criticise, expand / contract. Pairs are easier to remember than single words because each word reminds you of the other. Group the pairs by idea (size, speed, mood, honesty), and say them aloud. Before the test, revise the pairs that use prefixes, because those are the easiest marks to win back.
Remember that the answer is often a plain word. Examiners make the stem hard and the answer simple, so do not reject an option just because it looks too easy.

Pick the one that reverses the main sense, at the same strength. For FURIOUS the best opposite is calm, not merely pleased, because furious describes anger, not happiness. For SCARCE, the opposite is plentiful (amount), not cheap (price), even though scarce things are often costly.
! Read the stem's part of speech. The opposite of the verb RISE is fall or sink; the noun "fall" works only if it is the same class as the stem.
! Do not choose a word that is only different. For TIMID, "angry" is different, but bold is opposite.
! Words with two meanings: FAST can mean quick or firmly fixed. If the options include slow, the speed sense is being tested.
- Expect a synonym among the wrong options.
- Use prefixes and suffixes, but beware of inflammable and invaluable.
- Choose the option that reverses the main sense at the same strength.
